body.estimand_functional: \(g_{\chi}(C_{\le R})=\beta=C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,Y]/C_{d_{\chi}+2}[f_{\chi},T,T]\) for \(\chi\in\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{\ell,R}\) and \(C_{\le R}\in\mathcal U_{\chi}\); otherwise \(g_{\chi}(C_{\le R})=\bot\)

sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. sampling from one fixed member of \(\mathcal M_{\ell}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention target is the structural edge coefficient \(\beta\) on \(T\to Y\); treatment is not randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is used; regular inference is reported only when the deterministic selector returns an established chart whose discriminant is nonzero, while confidence-fiber inversion remains total at chart collisions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate all entries of \(C_{\le R}\) by multivariate \(k\)-statistics. The fixed degree-then-lexicographic selector returns \(\chi_n,d_n,\widehat\beta_n\) only on their declared established-chart domain and returns \(\bot\) otherwise. For collision-robust inversion, compute \(\widehat\mu_R\), \(\rho_n\), \(Q_n\), the possibly empty legal intersection \(\mathcal J_n\), the total projected set \(I_n\), and \(\eta_n\) from the finite atomic quantified-real presentation of \(\Theta_{\ell,R}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 3.4--3.5 identify the proxy-model effect from cumulants through \(k(\ell)\).
Specializing Theorems 3.4--3.5 to three latent confounders gives the sufficient input order \(k(3)=7\).
Theorem 3.6 claims order-three nonidentification for \(\ell=1\) after computing the vanishing ideal of the complete modified map and obtaining a quadratic in the effect coordinate.
Theorem 4 gives a degree-\(\ell+1\) bivariate loading polynomial whose coefficients use higher-order cumulants.
Propositions 3--4 give elimination-ideal criteria for generic identifiability of a target coordinate.
The paper gives cross-moment effect formulas in a one-confounder proxy setting and a Gaussian impossibility result.
Theorem 3.8 characterizes full-law effect identifiability in lvLiNGAM through overcomplete ICA.
Theorems 1.5 and 1.9 characterize full-distribution overcomplete-ICA mixing identifiability.
The paper develops tests for algebraic cumulant-rank constraints using incomplete \(U\)-statistics.
The paper constructs identification- and singularity-robust confidence sets for nonlinear moment-condition models.
The paper projects inverted causal-model tests to retain structural uncertainty.
The paper identifies causal effects from a single proxy under a known proxy mechanism.

body.tldr: Higher-order cumulants identify the treatment effect in a single-proxy latent-confounded LiNGAM, but the published order \(k(\ell)\) is only sufficient. The project characterizes the exact least depth \(r_{\beta}(\ell)\) over nonempty fibers on relatively Zariski-open subsets of the explicitly quantified legal observable image, combining a terminating proxy-anchored annihilator atlas above the frontier with open sets of real finite-support unequal-effect twins below it. The exact three-latent result changes the Tramontano et al. workflow from cumulants through \(k(3)=7\) to the sharp order four and requires a nonidentification report at order three on the open lower-fiber locus. Their one-latent proof correctly computes the vanishing ideal of the complete modified order-three map, but its quadratic algebraic projection does not enforce positive source variances and simultaneous centered truncated-moment realizability; the correction supplies an exact real-feasibility certificate and domain-indexed three-atom charts. The all-\(\ell\) kernel retains the mandatory complete \(\ell=2,R=3\) decision. Every scalar recovery and chart-selection construction is totalized by the common value \(\bot\) outside its proved domain; an established separated chart yields the \(k\)-statistic limit, while a total, possibly empty confidence-fiber projection gives uniform coverage, an \(n^{-1/2}\) radius, and collision-aware diameter bounds.

project_justification.gap: The nearest paper proves identification from pairwise cumulant roots through \(k(\ell)\) and claims a one-latent order-three lower result; it does not determine the minimum information depth of the complete ternary law, and its algebraic projection argument does not restrict the extra root to realizable centered source moments with positive variances.
project_justification.niche: The graph creates a distinguished proxy-zero pair of noise columns, so homogeneous forms annihilating only the sources entering \(Z\) can identify \(\beta\) before the entire overcomplete mixing matrix is recoverable.
project_justification.fill: The paper will provide the exact finite-\(\ell\) depth on the finite-atomic quantified-real observable image, a finite established rational atlas with explicit nonvanishing domains and a common failure output off those domains, legal-real converse fibers at all lower orders, an auditable real-infeasibility certificate for the additional one-latent algebraic root, and inference that switches from a proved separated Wald chart to total confidence-fiber inversion at the discriminant. At \(\ell=3\), the exact theorem replaces the published sufficient input \(C_{\le7}\) by the sharp \(C_{\le4}\) requirement and rules out point identification from \(C_{\le3}\) on the stated open locus.

body.related_work: Tramontano et al. (2025, Theorems 3.4--3.5) recover pairwise loading-root lists through \(k(\ell)\) and align them by source cumulants; Theorem 2 is a strict tightening because its complete-tensor contraction identifies on the covered relatively Zariski-open part of the same legal observable image at \(U_{\ell}<k(\ell)\), with an explicit failure output elsewhere. At \(\ell=3\), their sufficient workflow uses \(k(3)=7\), whereas Theorem 5 proves that order four is both sufficient and minimal on the stated generic legal loci; this removes orders five through seven from the workflow and changes the order-three output from a selected point to nonidentification. The proof of their Theorem 3.6 parameterizes the complete modified order-three cumulant map and computes its vanishing ideal; Theorem 3 accepts that algebraic calculation and isolates the domain gap: a second root of the projected quadratic must lift to a real graph point whose diagonal order-two cumulants are positive variances and whose order-two--three coordinates have a common centered representing law. The exact real-infeasibility certificate excludes only the additional branch under these legal restrictions and supplies explicitly domain-indexed positive three-atom charts for the retained branch and covariance twins. Schkoda, Robeva, and Drton (2024, Theorem 4) supplies higher-cumulant rank matrices and annihilating polynomials for bivariate latent LiNGAM, but does not classify the simultaneous ternary beta projection. Garcia-Puente, Spielvogel, and Sullivant (2010, Propositions 3--4) supplies the target-elimination framework adapted by the exact-frontier handle. Tramontano et al. (2024, Theorem 3.8) and Wang and Seigal (2026, Theorems 1.5 and 1.9) concern full-distribution effect or mixing identification, leaving finite truncation depth open. Kivva, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2023) is the scalar cross-moment precursor. Schkoda and Drton (2025), Andrews and Guggenberger (2019), and Strieder et al. (2021) inform, respectively, cumulant-rank testing, singular moment inference, and projected causal-model inversion. Vollmer, Pfister, and Weichwald (2026) identify effects with a single proxy under a known proxy mechanism and therefore do not subsume the unknown-mechanism non-Gaussian graph studied here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The contraction discriminant is initially a certificate-failure locus, not yet the true nonidentification locus. Accordingly, every chart-specific scalar construction returns \(\bot\) when its atlas is empty, its pivot or denominator vanishes, or its input lies outside the chart domain; no value on that failure locus is interpreted as an effect. The exact \(\ell=2,R=3\) real beta projection under the quantified finite-atomic source-moment constraints is the mandatory early decision. Complex fiber degree, Jacobian rank, failure of one annihilator, an unrestricted diagonal-cumulant solution, and a single finite-support witness are each insufficient for the global converse. The order-three algebraic image closure permits diagonal cumulant coordinates that need not be positive-variance centered source moments; polynomial degree alone therefore does not count legal preimages. Uniform confidence-fiber coverage uses the explicit observed-data envelope \(\lVert X\rVert_{\infty}\le M\); no observed bound is inferred from bounded latent sources or bounded disturbances with unrestricted structural coefficients. Off the simultaneous moment-coverage event the legal intersection and projected set may be empty and are reported as such. At an exact collision, honest coverage need not imply singleton contraction, and the limiting diameter is the legal-fiber modulus rather than a Wald rate.
body.honest_scope: The full-fiber contraction identity, improved upper depth, one- and three-latent exact cases, and weight-saturation lower region are theorem obligations supported by symbolic presolve but remain to be proved independently. The three-latent obligation has the independent operational content that \(C_{\le4}\), rather than the published sufficient \(C_{\le7}\), is the sharp generic input and that \(C_{\le3}\) cannot support a point-effect report on the open lower-fiber locus. The one-latent obligation reproduces the published complete modified-map vanishing ideal and then audits the additional quadratic branch only against the positive-variance, centered finite-atomic truncated-moment domain; it does not allege that the published elimination omitted cumulant equations. The exact finite-\(\ell\) frontier and global real-feasible lower-fiber theorem are the first-class open content, with the complete \(\ell=2,R=3\) legal beta projection under the same quantified-real domain as the mandatory early kill test. Uniform inference is confined to an observed-data envelope class. Wald output exists only on a proved established-chart domain and is \(\bot\) otherwise; confidence-fiber inversion is total, may return the empty set off coverage, and remains set-valued at unidentified collisions. When \(\ell=0\), the construction reduces to the standard covariance residualization formula. The bivariate causal-direction minimal-order frontier is a different object: it orients an arrow from two observed variables, whereas this project fixes the proxy graph and identifies one interventional coefficient from the complete trivariate cumulant map.
